judgment.rationale: B1.4.7.1 'Write simple compositions' (Sub-Strand 7: Controlled Writing) and B1.4.4.1 'Draw and label simple objects' (Sub-Strand 4: Labelling Items) are both BASIC 1 (rank 0, resolved Grade coordinate) Content Standards under STRAND 4: WRITING, so the statement-type grain matches and the rank gap is 0. They show genuine pair-specific coherence as complementary facets of early written production in the same grade: labelling drawings with invented spelling (indicator B1.4.4.1.1: draw simple pictures of peers or objects and use invented spelling to write about oneself) and producing simple compositions via controlled sentence work (indicator B1.4.7.1.1: find, read and copy sentences from a given substitution table). Practising either reinforces letter formation, word/sentence conventions, and the idea of recording meaning in writing, which is substantive instructional coherence rather than mere repeated wording. However, no developmental dependency is supported: the standards sit in parallel same-grade sub-strands, and the controlled-writing exemplar is a scaffolded copying task rather than a clear extension of independent invented-spelling labelling, so same-rank buildsTowards in either direction lacks the required substantive evidence. Nomination signals (single shared token 'simple', trigram overlap of that same token, weak b1|4 code prefix, shared Grade/Strand ancestors) are explicitly non-probative for direction. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and neither carries Learning Components.

This is more than the shared 'stories' token/code-prefix/page-proximity signals that nominated the pair. judgment.rationale: Both indicators sit in BASIC 2 (rank 1), Strand 4 Writing, and target the same content domain of objects found in the environment. B2.4.4.1.1 (Sub-Strand 4: Labelling Items; parent standard 'Draw and label simple pictures') requires learners to draw and label environmental objects, i.e. word-level naming/writing tied to concrete referents (LCs: 'Draw objects found in their environment', 'Label objects found in their environment'). B2.4.5.1.2 (Sub-Strand 5: Writing Simple Words and Sentences; parent standard 'Use knowledge of grammar and vocabulary to write words and sentences correctly') requires writing simple and meaningful sentences about the same objects. Proficiency in naming/labelling environmental objects supplies the vocabulary and object-referent base that supports success in composing sentences about those objects, so the direction is from the labelling indicator to the sentence-writing indicator (second_to_first), a substantive word-to-sentence expansion rather than repeated wording alone. Same-rank direction rests on this capability expansion, not on code or page proximity; endpoint source evidence is truncated, so the judgment uses the available statement text, LCs, and hierarchy only.
